rows.abstract: This bill seeks to grant board, lodging and/or housing benefits to ECOZONE employees and personnel.  It aims to redress the primary quandary of an ECOZONE employee who has been forced by circumstances to be away from the comforts of his home.  It likewise addresses the need of a similar employee who may have long wanted to have a place, proximate to where he works, his new home, but may not afford to buy it.  In a simple way, it seeks to balance the welfare of these laborers with their employers.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `HOSPITAL LICENSURE ACT'
rows.abstract: Rationale: More than 20 years have passed since its enactment the provisions of the R.A. 4226 "Hospital Licensure Act" are rendered absolute and "without teeth". Its penal provisions are weak in charter, thus, hospitals found violating the same havemanaged to continue operating by merely paying a fine the amount of Five hundred pesos (P500). Moreover, the Bureau of licensing and Regulation (BLR) does not exercise quasi-judicial functions over violations of the Act.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Since the advent of urbanization, squatting has been a pervasive that society had to contend with. It is sad to note, however, that from the end of the Marcos regime to the assumption of then President Corazon C. Aquino, the squatting menace has grown and is still with us.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE MANNER OF ELECTION OF THE MEMBERS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE PHILIPPINE VETERANS BANK AND AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-FIVE HUNDRED AND EIGHTEEN AND REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE
rows.abstract: This bill prescribes a new system or manner in the election of the Board of Directors of the Bank and strips the Board of the Veterans of World WarII of the authority to vote for the issued but undelivered shares of the Bank. The system will serve to satisfy the desire of the stockholders for fairness and equity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-07-25

rows.abstract: The bill proposes the creation of a veterans agency to be known as the Philippine Veterans Authority, a cabinet-level body which shall perform governmental and proprietary functions towrds ensuring the provision of immediate and adequate care, benefits and other forms of assistance to veterans and their dependents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE RELEASE OF FUNDS DIRECTLY TO THE SANGGUNIANG BARANGAY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 329 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of  1991, states that "ten percent (10%) of the general fund of the barangay shall be alloted for the Sangguniang Kabataan." This statutory mandate, however, is more often honored in the breach than in its enforcement because most Sangguniang Barangays generally consider it wiser to use scarce financial resources on projects and activities that are deemed "of greater benefit to the barangay" than SK concerns. Thus, funds which are, by law intended for the youth are channeled to other purposes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING BENEFITS TO COLLEGE AND POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Some benefits proposed in this bill are: (1) Initial bank deposit of P500.00; (2) transportation fare discount; (3) textbook discount; (4) medical and dental services discount, etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-25

rows.author: C137
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 99 AND 262 OR BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Omnibus Election Code (RA 7166) failed to DECRIMINALIZE those acts with respect to persons making contributions to electoral candidates/poli tical parties. The bill, therefore seeks to remedy the situation by DECRIMINALIZING violations of Sections 98 and 99 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 881, As Amended, otherwise known as the "Omnibus Election Code."  The bill, nevertheless imposes on persons who violate these sections administrative fines similar to those provided in Section 14 of Republic Act No. 7166 which are imposed on candidates and political parties who fail to file a report on campaign contributions and expenditures. In addition to the fines, a contributor who fails to comply with Section 98 and 99 will not be able to claimm exemption from gift tax.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06418

rows.author: D063
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09282) enacted on 2004-03-30
rows.title_full: AN ACT ELEVATING THE RANK OF THE COURT OF TAX APPEALS (CTA) TO THE LEVEL OF A COLLEGIATE COURT WITH SPECIAL JURISDICTION, ENLARGING ITS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, EXPANDING ITS JURISDICTION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1125, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LAW CREATING THE COURT OF TAX APPEALS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Presently, the jurisdiction over criminal cases involving violations of the tax and customs laws is lodged with the regular courts, while the civil aspect of these cases is with the Coirt of Tax Appeals, thus resulting into needless delays in the final disposition of cases. Moreover, this delay is further prolonged by the appeal of the cases cognizable by the Court of Tax Appeals to the Court of Appeals.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06673

rows.author: D063
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOCATING TO THE AFP MODERNIZATION ACT TRUST FUND THE COLLECTION FROM CAPITAL GAINS TAX AND VALUE-ADDED TAX ON THE SALE OF REAL PROPERTY AND THE SHARE OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT ON ALL TAXES, ROYALTIES AND CHARGES COLLECTED FROM THE MALAMPAYA NATURAL GAS PROJECT
rows.abstract: To date, there has not been much progress in the implementation of the Program. Major weapon and non-weapon equipment and technology acquisition as well as major infrastructure construction and/or improvement entail huge sums of money which cannot be supported by the trust fund alone. Thus, other sources should be tapped to augment the limited sources of the Trust Fund.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D063
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A SEVEN PERCENT (7%) COMPUTER EDUCATION TAX ON RECEIPTS (EXCLUDING VALUE-ADDED TAX) FROM CELLULAR PHONE CALLS TO BE BORNE BY CELLULAR PHONE COMPANIES, CREATING A SPECIAL COMPUTER LITERACY EDUCATION FUND FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: There shall be levied, assessed and collected on receipts (excluding value-added tax) from cellular phone calls a computer eduction tax amounting to seven percent (7%) to be borne by each cellular company from the effectivity of the Act. Receipts from cellular phone calls shall mean revenues made by cellular companies from prepaid cellphone cards, text messaging service, post-paid calls and other services using the cellular network. This tax shall be in addition to, and separate from the incomeand value-added taxes a cellular company remits to the bureau of Internal Revenue.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D063
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING PREPARATORY EDUCATION AS COMPULSORY PART OF BASIC PRIMARY EDUCATION IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed measure seeks to lay down an equitable situation for our preschool children.It seeks to institutionaliz e preparatory education to five-year old children as part of compulsory education before Grade I to be provided by the National Government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: D063
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR OPTIMUM PERFORMANCE IN REVENUE COLLECTION THROUGH LATERAL ATTRITION AND GRANTING OF SPECIAL INCENTIVES AND REWARDS FOR EXEMPLARY SERVICE IN REVENUE-GENERAT ING AGENCIES OF GOVERNMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The issue of graft and corruption in revenue-generat ing agencies and/or local government units must be acted upon resolutely, however, radically. At the same time, collections in the respective areas of responsibility of revenue and customs officers/offici als and local government treasurers/assi stant treasurers must be increased or maintained at the very least. This bill would allow expeditious action against non-performing officers/offici als by removing them from their positionsif they do not come up to the set standards like the achievement of target collection goals. In contrast, it is also proposed in this Act to award special incentives and rewards to officers/offici als who render exemplary  and honest performance intheir revenue-collect ion.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04594

rows.author: D063
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE FEES AND CHARGES ON FIREARMS, AMMUNITION, SPARE PARTS, ACCESSORIES, COMPONENTS, EXPLOSIVES, EXPLOSIVE INGREDIENTS, PYROTECHNICS AND FIRECRACKERS
rows.abstract: The Philippine National Police, in its bid to modernize its services and professionalize its officials and personnel, needs the much-needed support in terms of appropriations from the national government. This bill aims to plug this open loophole and provide the PNP a discretion to retain and use its collected revenues from its regulatory functions such as licensing, registration, and issuance of permits. It rationalizes the fees and charges of firearms, ammunition, spare parts, accessories, components, explosives, explosive ingredients, pyrotechnics and firecrackers to more realistic rates with consideration of industry concerns.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2001-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT LEGALIZING DIVORCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE TITLE II AND ARTICLES 55 TO 57 THEREUNDER OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Executive Order No. 209, otherwise known as the Family Code of the Philippines, as amended by Executive Order No. 227, by allowing absolute divorce (a vinculo matrimonii) and thereby granting legally separated spouses the right to remarry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING CRISIS INTERVENTION CENTERS FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS AND SURVIVORS OF ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: These Centers shall provide support for for women and children in order to help women gain the necessary skills and knowledge to become self-sufficient and productive members of society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INTEGRATE COMPUTER EDUCATION INTO THE ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY CURRICULUM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: It shall be mandatory for all elementary and secondary schools to integrate computer education in their curricula.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RATIONALIZE THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF ALL LAWS ON OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH STANDARDS AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Studies show that there are a number of government agencies, both national and local, that are involved in the administration and enforcement of occupational safety and health and environmental protection laws. It appears that these agencies are authorized by existing laws to participate in the implementation of these concerns.> Studies moreover show that there is no single lead agency that coordinates and oversees the implementation of the national program on occupational safety andhealth and the environmental protection thereby resulting in the fragmented administration of said programs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT RENAMING THE NATIONAL HISTORICAL INSTITUTE (NHI) TO NATIONAL HISTORICAL COMMISSION (NHC), INSTITUTIONALIZ ING REORGANIZATION THEREOF, PROVIDING FOR IMPROVEMENT AND STRENGTHENING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to change the name of the Naitonal Historical Institute (NHI) to National Historical Commission thereby institutionaliz ing reorganizationa l changes and strengthening its mandate as the country's primary institution responsible for the preservation and promotion of Philippine history. Considering the financial limitations of the organization, this bills seeks to professionalize and streamline the prevailing bureaucratic structure of the NHI by decreasing the number of peopleconstituting its Board and designating the Board's Chairperson to act in concurrent capacity as the NHC Executive Director.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09241) enacted on 2004-02-10
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF THE NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE PROGRAM BY INCLUDING THEREIN HOME CARE AND REHABILITATION SERVICES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7875, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE ACT OF 1995,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: With the fast changing social and economic environment environment, our country is faced with the problem of meeting the health needs of its increasing population. Hence. there is a need to develop a less expensive but comprehensive and continuing care and rehabilitation program for patients upon their discharge from the hospital to a more suitable and familiar environment-the home.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05547

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO PRIVATE HOSPITALS BY GRANTING INCENTIVES AND ESTABLISHING A PRIVATE-HOSPITA L DEVELOPMENT PLAN
rows.abstract: This legislation proposes a Private Hospital Development Plan, which will be drawn in coordination with the Secretary of Health, appropriate government agencies and non-government organizations. This plan shall monitor the needs of private hospitalsin terms of its facilities, equipment and human resources. It shall also grant tax incentives to accredited private hospitals.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-05-21, transmitted to on 2003-05-22 and received by the Senate on 2003-05-27
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INCENTIVES TO SUBDIVISION HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATIONS TO DEVELOP AND MAINTAIN FORESTED AREAS WITHIN THEIR SUBDIVISIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Green Parks Act of 2001." This bill seeks to expand the area to be devoted to the preservation of the ecological balance of nature. In reserving a whole area for such activity, and by getting the community members involved, it is hoped that there would eventually be a sincere appreciation for a healthy, clean and natural environment.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05812

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE AND ENCOURAGE THE FORMATION AND OPERATION OF PRIVATE NONPROFIT EMERGENCY RESCUE UNITS (RE:  GOOD SAMARITAN ACT OF 2001)
rows.abstract: "Good Samaritan Act of 2001." This bill seeks to address the confluence of constitutional concerns for public safety, health, and, in general, the value of human life by making it a State policy to promote and encourage the formation and operation of private non-profit emergency rescue units, and prescribing the mechanics for government assistance and support.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROGRAM FOR THE REDUCTION OF THE TEACHER TO STUDENTS RATIO IN THE PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: There shall be established a Teacher-Student s Radio Reduction Program, hereinafter called Program, which shall effectively reduce the actual classroom-teach er to student ratio to an ideal proportion of at least one teacher for every thirty (30) students.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL BRANCHES, SUBDIVISIONS, INSTRUMENTALITI ES AND AGENCIES OF THE GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNE D OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS OR THEIR SUBSIDIARIES TO DIVULGE THE IDENTITY OF HIRED FOREIGN CONSULTANTS, THE NATURE OF THEIR WORK AND THEIR COMPENSATIONS, PERKS, AND OTHER PRIVILEGES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES IN CASE OF VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to require full disclosure of the identity, nature of work, and compensation of foreign consultants hired or retained by the Government, its agencies, instrumentaliti es, including government-owne d or-controlled corporations. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1566, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE DISASTER CONTROL, CAPABILITY AND ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL PROGRAM ON COMMUNITY DISASTER PREPAREDNESS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to transfer the chairmanship of the National Disaster Coordinating Council from the Department of National Defense to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Furthermore, it mandates that the Executive Officer of theNational Disaster Coordinating Council shall be the Director of the Bureau of Emergency Assistance of the DSWD.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A PROGRAM FOR THE CONTINUING EDUCATION OF COLLEGE TEACHERS, AMENDING FOR SUCH PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7784, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT STRENGTHENING TEACHER EDUCATION IN THE PHILIPPINES BY ESTABLISHING CENTERS FOR EXCELLENCE, CREATING A TEACHER EDUCATION COUNCIL FOR THE PURPOSE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: ALL PRIMARY, SECONDARY AND COLLEGE TEACHERS SHALL UNDERGO TRAINING IN PROFESSIONAL EDUCATION, GENERAL EDUCATION AND TEACHING METHODS IN THEIR FIELDS OF SPECIALIZATION AT LEAST ONCE EVERY FIVE (5) YEARS TO BE HELD DURING SCHOOL BREAKS. ANY TEACHER WHO FAILS TO UNDERGO OR COMPLETE THE SAID TRAINING SHALL NOT BE GIVEN ANY TEACHING LOAD FOR A PERIOD OF FIVE (5) YEARS FROM THE DATE OF COMPLETION OF THE NEXT TRAINING. THE RESULTS OF THE TRAINING PROGRAM SHALL ALSO BE THE BASIS FOR THE PROMOTION OF TEACHERS AND THE AMOUNT OF TEACHING LOADS TO BE ALLOCATED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO PRIVATE HOSPITALS BY GRANTING INCENTIVES AND ESTABLISHING A PRIVATE HOSPITAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN
rows.abstract: Rationale: Private hospitals comprise 70.5% of the country's total number of hospitals. The government should help make the operations of these hospitals economically viable since the quality of service depend on the viability of their operations. Discontinuance of services by any hospital due to financial failure means an added drain on the scarce health resources of the government. More importantly, government assistance to private hospitals will help make hospital costs more affordable. Incentives to hospital dispersal to underserved/uns erved areas will likewise make health services accessible to the people.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTOMATICALLY INCLUDING RETIRED SCHOOL TEACHERS TO BENEFIT FROM SALARY INCREASES GRANTED TO IN-SERVE TEACHERS, EFFECTING CORRESPONDING ADJUSTMENTS IN THEIR RETIREMENT PENSION
rows.abstract: Retired schoolteachers are hereby automatically included to benefit from salary increases granted to in-service teachers as a result of which, corresponding adjustments shall be made in their retirement pension.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO GRANT PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS FREE OF CHARGE X-RAY AND OTHER FORMS OF LABORATORY EXAMINATIONS IN ANY GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE HOSPITALS DURING THEIR REQUIRED ANNUAL PHYSICAL EXAMINATION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: X-ray and other forms of laboratory examinations shall be granted to all public schoolteachers in any government and private hospitals. Provided, however, that such privilege shall only be available during the required annual physical examination schedule.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES TO PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO ARE ASSIGNED OUTSIDE OF THEIR TOWNS AND PROVINCES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any public schoolteacher who is assigned to a town other that his own, shall, in addition to his basic salary and benefits under the Salary Standardization Law, be entitled to One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00) monthly as incentive allowance.> Any public schoolteacher who is assigned to a town of another than his own, shall, in addition to his basic salary and benefits under the Salary Standardization Law  be entitled to receive Two Thousand Pesos (P2,000.00) a month as incentive allowance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MINIMUM SUBSISTENCE ALLOWANCE FOR BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 6 (b) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7883, ENTITLED `AN ACT GRANTING BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES TO ACCREDITED BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS AND FOR OTHERPURPOSES'
rows.abstract: "(b) Subsistence Allowance - Barangay health workers who render service within the premises of isolated barangay health stations in order to make their services available at any and all times, shall be entitled to a monthly subsistence allowance, which shall be computed in accordance with prevailing circumstances as determined by the local government unit concerned, BUT SHALL IN NO CASE LESS THAN P1,000.00."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-07-25

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT DESIGNATING THE PHILIPPINE PHILHARMONIC ORCHESTRA AS THE NATIONAL ORCHESTRA OF THE PHILIPPINES, DEFINING ITS ROLE AND FUNCTIONS AS SUCH, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: In recognition of its efforts and numerous awards it has received for and in behalf of the Philippines, the attached measure seeks to designate the Philippine Philharmonic Orchestra (PPO) as the country's national orchestra. The bill grants the orchestra and its members certain benefits, such as exemption from civil service laws; free use of office space, rehearsal studios, and production and technical facilities at the CCP; and travel and project grants for research, documentation,and production from the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-25

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-03-06, transmitted to on 2002-03-11 and received by the Senate on 2002-03-12
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE EXEMPTION OF FIXED INCOME EARNERS FROM THE FILING OF INCOME TAX RETURNS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 44, NO. 2 (C) OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 273, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is submitted that the work involved for both taxpayers and the government in the filing of these returns would be considerably lessened if fixed income earners were exempted from the filing of income tax returns. Since their income taxes are already withheld by their employers, the filing of income tax returns of fixed income is an exercise in futility. For these fixed income earners, the certificates of withholding income may serve as proof of income, in lieu of income tax returns.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04111
